statusDefinitions.IMPLEMENTED_RUNTIME_PENDING: Implementation and tests are versioned, but exact-SHA deployed runtime evidence is not yet accepted.
statusDefinitions.IMPLEMENTED_EVIDENCE_REVALIDATION_REQUIR: Implementation and registered evidence exist, but the evidence must be revalidated for the assessed SHA.
statusDefinitions.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED: The product workflow exists, but qualified human review remains a mandatory boundary.
statusDefinitions.NOT_APPLICABLE: The row is deliberately outside the legal-obligation mapping and includes a justification.

entries.obligation: Take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy for staff and other persons operating or using AI systems on the organisation's behalf.
entries.applicability: Applicable from 2025-02-02 where the organisation acts as provider or deployer.
entries.limitation: The platform records literacy operations and evidence; it does not determine whether a customer's measures are legally sufficient for every context.

entries.paragraph: Article 5(1), excluding the 2026 points mapped separately below
entries.obligation: Prevent prohibited AI practices and preserve evidence, exception analysis and accountable decisions.
entries.applicability: Applicable from 2025-02-02, subject to the precise statutory conditions and exceptions.
entries.limitation: A workflow decision is not a legal determination; exceptions and contested facts require qualified review.

entries.paragraph: Article 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b)
entries.obligation: Address prohibited generation or manipulation of non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material when the amended statutory conditions are met.
entries.applicability: The amending regulation entered into force on 2026-07-27; these provisions apply from 2026-12-02.
entries.limitation: The repository placeholder is deliberately non-creditable until an exact deployed SHA produces a PASS artifact; factual purpose, safeguards, consent and 'without right' analysis remain human-review boundaries.
entries.sourceVersion: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1(7) and amended Article 113; legal-rules version 2026-07-30.1

entries.paragraph: Risk management and data/data-governance requirements for high-risk systems
entries.obligation: Operate risk-management and data-governance controls proportionate to the applicable high-risk system.
entries.applicability: Applicable only when the system is legally classified as high-risk and the relevant provider duties are in application.
entries.limitation: The deterministic workspace is evidence-preparation support and does not establish legal high-risk classification or dataset adequacy by itself.

entries.obligation: Prepare and maintain technical documentation for applicable high-risk AI systems.
entries.applicability: Applicable to providers of high-risk AI systems, subject to the amended application timeline.
entries.limitation: Generated structure must be completed and reviewed against the actual system, intended purpose, changes and applicable standards.

entries.paragraph: Record-keeping, transparency to deployers, human oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
entries.obligation: Support logs, instructions, oversight and technical control evidence for applicable high-risk systems.
entries.applicability: Role-specific and applicable only to systems within the relevant high-risk scope.
entries.limitation: Technical evidence does not prove that real-world model performance or human oversight is adequate for a customer's deployment.

entries.obligation: Maintain a documented quality management system for applicable high-risk AI systems.
entries.applicability: Applicable to providers within the high-risk framework, subject to proportionality and amended implementation dates.
entries.limitation: The product organises QMS evidence; operational adoption and effectiveness require organisational execution and review.

entries.obligation: Operate applicable deployer controls, including instructions, oversight, monitoring, logs and escalation.
entries.applicability: Applicable to deployers of high-risk systems, with role- and context-specific duties.
entries.limitation: Applicability and sufficiency depend on actual deployment facts, instructions, local law and organisational execution.

entries.obligation: Perform a fundamental-rights impact assessment where Article 27 applies.
entries.applicability: Required only for the deployers and use cases specified in Article 27; uncertain cases remain under review.
entries.limitation: Rights impact, affected groups, residual impact and legal applicability require qualified review and stakeholder-specific facts.

entries.obligation: Support applicable disclosures, labelling and machine-readable marking for interactive and synthetic-content use cases.
entries.applicability: Role-, system- and content-specific; general Article 50 application begins on 2026-08-02.
entries.limitation: The correct disclosure depends on role, content type, exceptions, technical feasibility and the actual user experience.
entries.sourceVersion: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 50, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

entries.obligation: For qualifying synthetic-content systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02, take necessary steps to comply with Article 50(2) by 2026-12-02.
entries.applicability: Provider-only transition; not a transition for deployer obligations under Article 50(4).
entries.limitation: Qualification as a pre-existing provider system requires factual and legal confirmation; the exact-SHA runtime artifact is still pending.

entries.obligation: Support applicable GPAI documentation, downstream information, copyright, training-content summary and systemic-risk controls.
entries.applicability: Applicable only where the organisation is legally a GPAI model provider; thresholds and open-source exceptions require review.
functionality: GPAI compliance workspace and evidence model
entries.limitation: The platform cannot establish GPAI role, systemic-risk designation, copyright compliance or model-level technical sufficiency without qualified evidence.

entries.obligation: Maintain legal-source freshness and avoid treating superseded, unpublished or not-yet-applicable rules as current obligations.
entries.applicability: Product governance control supporting legal-rule maintenance; not a transfer of the Commission's statutory review duty to customers.
entries.limitation: This is an internal product governance mapping. It does not purport to perform the institutional review assigned to EU bodies.

entries.paragraph: Platform security, deployment, backup, restore and release gates
entries.obligation: No single EU AI Act article is asserted for the generic SaaS platform controls in this row.
entries.applicability: NOT_APPLICABLE — these are cross-cutting engineering and operational controls, not a direct article-to-feature legal claim.
entries.limitation: These controls may support security, accountability and evidence quality, but this registry does not invent a direct legal obligation mapping for them.
